samples.summary: DOCX export still interpolates untrusted color values into XML attributes unescaped — the same injection class this diff fixes for `headingLevel`, left open for `w:color` / `w:shd w:fill`
samples.evidence:
The diff's own rationale (docx-style-map.ts:96-102) is that block/inline attrs "reach export from untrusted input (the internal clipboard payload, DOCX/HTML/PPTX imports)" and must not be interpolated raw into an attribute value. `headingLevel` is now coerced, but the color sinks in the same file are untouched and reachable by exactly the same route:

1. Sink: `docx-style-map.ts:73` `parts.push(`<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` and :77 `<w:shd ... w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"/>`; plus `docx-exporter.ts:311` `<w:shd ... w:fill="${cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')}"/>`. None call `escapeXmlAttr` (the helper defined at docx-style-map.ts:25 and used only for `fontFamily`). `.replace('#','')` strips one hash, nothing else.
2. Source: `defaultColorResolver` (model/color.ts:16) returns a string `StoredColor` verbatim, and the NEW clipboard validator explicitly admits arbitrary strings — `asStoredColor` (view/clipboard.ts:91 `if (typeof value === 'string') return value;` and :94-95 `{kind:'srgb', value: <any string>}`) and `sanitizeCellStyle` (view/clipboard.ts:217 `asString(value.backgroundColor)`).
3. Attack: a hostile page's `copy` handler puts `application/x-waffledocs` JSON on the clipboard (the handler at view/text-editor.ts:1240 prefers this flavour over text/html); victim pastes, then exports DOCX. With `style.color = 'a" w:themeColor="x'` the emitted document.xml contains `<w:color w:val="a" w:themeColor="x"/>`; closing the element (`a"/>` …) permits arbitrary OOXML element injection inside the run (e.g. field codes), i.e. a crafted document the victim then distributes. The same value also arrives from a crafted .docx via import/docx-style-map.ts:264 (`color: `#${color}`` from an attacker-controlled `w:color` attribute).
For contrast, the slides PPTX exporter already escapes the analogous value (`slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35` `escapeXmlAttr(c.value…)`) and validates the role arm (pptx/text.ts:174), so the docs DOCX exporter is the outlier. Fix: escape (or hex-validate) colors, ideally both in `asStoredColor`/`sanitizeCellStyle` and at the three XML attribute sinks.

samples.summary: New clipboard validator bounds `listLevel`/`headingLevel` but leaves `tableData.rowHeights` unbounded, and that value is a hard row-height minimum that drives a per-page pagination loop — a pasted payload can hang every collaborator's tab
samples.evidence:
`sanitizeTableData` copies row heights straight through: `table.rowHeights = rows.map((_, r) => asNumber((value.rowHeights as unknown[])[r]))` (view/clipboard.ts:270-272); `asNumber` (clipboard.ts:69) accepts any finite number, with no ceiling (contrast MAX_LIST_LEVEL at :57 and the 1–6 clamp at :84-88, which show bounding was in scope).
That number is applied verbatim as a row-height minimum: `view/table-layout.ts:228-234` `if (userHeight !== undefined && userHeight > rowHeights[r]) rowHeights[r] = userHeight;`. Pagination then splits the row page-by-page: `view/pagination.ts:116-138` `while (consumed < rowHeight) { if (consumed > 0) startNewPage(); … consumed += fragHeight; }` where `fragHeight <= min(remaining, contentHeight)` (~800px). With `rowHeights: [1e12]` that is ~1e9 iterations, each pushing a `LayoutPage` and a `PageLine` → tab freeze / OOM.
Vector: hostile page writes the `application/x-waffledocs` flavour (preferred at view/text-editor.ts:1240) containing a table block with a huge `rowHeights` entry; victim pastes, the table is written into the shared Yorkie document, so the hang is persistent and reproduces for every collaborator who opens the doc, not just the pasting user. `columnWidths` (clipboard.ts:268) is likewise unbounded, though I only traced the unbounded loop for row heights.
searchedFor: read sanitizeTableData/asNumber in packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts for numeric ceilings
read packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts paginateLayout loops (while consumed < rowHeight)
grep normalizeTableMerges in model/types.ts for span clamping (spans ARE clamped; heights are not)
grep MAX_ constants in clipboard.ts (only MAX_LIST_LEVEL, MAX_TABLE_DEPTH)

samples.summary: The new validator applies no protocol/origin allowlist to `image.src` (or `href`), so a hostile clipboard payload persists an attacker URL into the shared document that every collaborator's browser then fetches
samples.evidence: `sanitizeImageData` accepts any string src (`const src = asString(value.src)`, view/clipboard.ts:112-115) and `sanitizeInlineStyle` any href (:148-149). `href` is at least gated at its sinks by `isSafeUrl` (view/text-editor.ts:1372, export/pdf-painter.ts:834, frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:183), but `image.src` is gated nowhere: `view/image-cache.ts:71` does `img.src = src` for rendering, and `frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:46-51` fetches it with `credentials: "include"` during PDF/DOCX export. Because paste writes the block into the shared Yorkie tree, an attacker-crafted `application/x-waffledocs` payload (preferred at view/text-editor.ts:1240) turns into a persistent beacon: every collaborator who opens the document issues a request to the attacker's host (IP/UA/timing disclosure), and an unbounded `data:` src is a memory sink. This is not a regression introduced here (the old code cast the payload wholesale, and HTML paste also copies ``), but the new key-by-key validator is the natural place for a `SAFE_PROTOCOLS`-style check and did not add one.
searchedFor: grep isSafeUrl across packages (found href gates; no image.src gate)
grep image.src / \.src\b in packages/docs/src (image-cache.ts:71, paint-layout.ts:365, docx/pdf exporters)
grep imageFetcher in packages/frontend/src → export-utils.ts docsImageFetcher fetch(credentials:'include')
read packages/core/src/url/index.ts isSafeUrl + core/test/url.test.ts for the existing allowlist

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. sanitizeTableData (clipboard.ts:255-273) passes rowHeights/columnWidths through asNumber (clipboard.ts:69-71), which accepts any finite number with no ceiling, while the same function clamps listLevel (MAX_LIST_LEVEL :57/:317), table depth (MAX_TABLE_DEPTH :59/:256), heading level (:84-88) and truncates spans (:238-241). I grepped every rowHeights use under packages/docs/src: downstream code only ever applies minimums (table-layout.ts:220-235 uses the value as a floor; table-resize.ts:146 sets maxPixel: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; document.ts:845-849 and store/memory.ts:195-199 store it unchanged) — no MAX_ROW_HEIGHT, normalizer, or iteration cap exists anywhere. The value survives the paste path intact: text-editor.ts:1240-1254 prefers the attacker-writable WAFFLEDOCS_MIME flavour, and cloneBlockWithFreshIds (block-helpers.ts:143-169) is a JSON deep clone that only rewrites ids. pagination.ts:116-138 then splits the row page-by-page with fragHeight bounded by contentHeight and no loop guard, so a rowHeights entry of ~1e12 produces ~1e9 iterations each allocating a LayoutPage/PageLine → tab freeze/OOM, persisted to the shared Yorkie doc so it reproduces for every collaborator. Unbounded numeric field in a deserializer of untrusted clipboard input; in-lane as unsafe input handling/deserialization with an availability impact.

finding.summary: DOCX export still interpolates attacker-controllable color strings into XML attributes unescaped, while the same function's headingLevel sink was hardened
finding.evidence:
This change hardened `headingLevel` at docx-style-map.ts:102 because "a string could otherwise close the quote and inject attributes", but the two sibling sinks in the same function are untouched: line 73 `parts.push(`<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` and line 77 `w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"`. `colorHex` comes from `defaultColorResolver`, which returns the stored value verbatim for the `string` and `{kind:'srgb'}` forms (model/color.ts:16-17) — no hex validation, and `<`, `>`, `"` are not escaped (`escapeXmlAttr` is applied only to fontFamily).

Two untrusted sources reach it, one of them the very path this diff set out to validate:
(a) the internal clipboard payload — the new sanitizer's `asStoredColor` returns any string as-is (`if (typeof value === 'string') return value;`, clipboard.ts:91) and accepts any string as an srgb `value` (clipboard.ts:94), so a hostile page's `application/x-waffledocs` payload with `style.color = 'FF0000"/><w:fldSimple w:instr=" DDEAUTO c:\\windows\\system32\\cmd.exe "/><w:color w:val="000000'` survives sanitization verbatim;
(b) DOCX import, which builds `style.color = `#${val}`` from an attacker-supplied `w:color/@w:val` with no validation (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62, and `#${color}` for borders at :264).
The value then lands unescaped in `word/document.xml`, allowing arbitrary OOXML element injection (field codes such as DDEAUTO / INCLUDEPICTURE for command execution or NTLM leakage) into a .docx the victim exports and typically forwards — or, minimally, a corrupt file Word refuses to open.

That this is an oversight rather than an accepted risk is visible in the sibling exporters, which do validate the same value: `pdf-style-map.ts:146` gates on `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i` and slides' PPTX writer escapes it (`escapeXmlAttr(c.value...)`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35). Fix: run colors through `escapeXmlAttr` and/or a `^#?[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` check on both the export side and in `asStored

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. docx-style-map.ts:71-78 interpolates `colorHex`/`bgHex` into `w:val`/`w:fill` XML attributes with only a `.replace('#','')` — quotes and angle brackets are not escaped, while `escapeXmlAttr` (defined at :25-32) is applied solely to font family at :53-56 and `headingLevel` was hardened at :95-103. `defaultColorResolver` (model/color.ts:14-22) returns the stored string / srgb `value` verbatim with no hex validation. Two untrusted sources reach it unvalidated: the clipboard sanitizer's `asStoredColor` (view/clipboard.ts:90-96) accepts any string, wired to `style.color`/`backgroundColor` at :154-157 (note it validates headingLevel strictly at :84-88, so the omission is asymmetric); and DOCX import builds `style.color = `#${val}`` from attacker-supplied `w:color/@w:val` (import/docx-style-map.ts:59-63) and `shd/@w:fill` (:73-77). The value is spliced raw into document.xml at export/docx-exporter.ts:217-222, where the adjacent text node IS escaped. The sibling PDF exporter validates the same value (`/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i`, pdf-style-map.ts:146), confirming this is an oversight. I found no guard anywhere on the path, so no refutation ground applies; this is in-lane injection / unsafe input handling into generated OOXML.

finding.summary: Table-cell backgroundColor from a clipboard payload is interpolated unescaped into <w:shd w:fill> in the exported DOCX
finding.evidence: `docx-exporter.ts:309-311` does `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')` and interpolates it straight into `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>` — no escaping, no hex validation. The newly added sanitizer accepts any string here: `sanitizeCellStyle` does `const backgroundColor = asString(value.backgroundColor); if (...) style.backgroundColor = backgroundColor;` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:217-218), and the `tableCells` half of the payload goes through the same function (clipboard.ts:355). Border colors take the same shape (`sanitizeBorder`, clipboard.ts:209) and DOCX import also produces `#${color}` unchecked (import/docx-style-map.ts:264). Attacker: hostile page puts a `application/x-waffledocs` payload on the clipboard with a table cell whose `backgroundColor` is `FFFFFF"/><w:injected …/><w:shd w:fill="FFFFFF`; the victim pastes and exports, producing attacker-chosen XML inside word/document.xml.

verdict.reason: Verified present and reachable. docx-exporter.ts:309-311 interpolates cell.style.backgroundColor into the w:fill attribute after only stripping the first '#', with no escaping or hex validation — while the sibling exporter module defines escapeXmlAttr (export/docx-style-map.ts:25-32) and applies it to fontFamily (:53-54) for exactly this reason, and documents the same untrusted-input attribute-injection risk at :96-102. The value is attacker-controlled: sanitizeCellStyle accepts any string (view/clipboard.ts:217-218 via asString at :65-67), and the tableCells half of the payload routes through it (clipboard.ts:355 -> sanitizeCellRows :245-253 -> sanitizeCell :235). The WAFFLEDOCS_MIME payload is writable by any page from its own copy handler (acknowledged in clipboard.ts:36-43) and is read preferentially in text-editor.ts:1240-1250, which calls pasteTableCells (text-editor.ts:3684-3741); cloneTableCells copies style verbatim (clipboard.ts:365) with no color normalization, so the raw string reaches the export sink. Vector: hostile page sets backgroundColor to 'FFFFFF"/><w:injected/><w:shd w:fill="FFFFFF', victim pastes and exports, producing attacker-chosen XML in word/document.xml. Border colors take the same unvalidated shape (clipboard.ts:209). Unsafe interpolation of untrusted input into generated markup is in the injection lane; no guard exists on any point of this path, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: BlockStyle.alignment is interpolated unescaped into <w:jc w:val="…"> and is read back from Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast
finding.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` interpolates the alignment verbatim: `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` (docx-style-map.ts:106-109). The clipboard path now allowlists it (`asOneOf(value.alignment, ALIGNMENTS)`, clipboard.ts:181), but the CRDT read path does not: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:222` does `if ('alignment' in attrs) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment'];` — a raw string cast from tree node attributes. A participant able to write raw Yorkie tree attributes for a shared document (edit-permission collaborator issuing a crafted update rather than using the UI) can therefore set `alignment` to `left"/><w:fldSimple w:instr="…"/><w:jc w:val="left` and inject XML/field codes into every other user's exported .docx. The canvas renderer only string-compares alignment, so nothing else rejects the value. I could not confirm a concrete non-UI write path for tree attrs, hence low confidence; the unescaped sink and the unchecked cast are both directly observable.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present exactly as described and the injection chain closes end-to-end. Sink: packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:106-108 interpolates `style.alignment` into `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` with no escaping — while the same file escapes `fontFamily` via escapeXmlAttr (lines 25-32, 53-56) and clamps `headingLevel` to an integer (lines 96-103) precisely because those "reach export from untrusted input", making alignment the inconsistent gap rather than an accepted pattern. Source: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:222 casts a raw CRDT tree attribute string via `attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` with no validation. I checked the most likely refutation — the normalizer at line 228 — and normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:280-282) is a bare `{...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style}` spread with no allowlist, so the tainted value survives. Reachability: yorkie-doc-store.ts:411/437 assign `style: parseBlockStyle(attrs)` to blocks, docx-exporter.ts:182-184 passes `block.style` into buildParagraphPropertiesXml, and docx-actions.ts:45 / docs-export-button.tsx:89 expose the export to users, so a crafted attribute lands in every collaborator's exported .docx. The other two untrusted entry points ARE allowlisted (import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107 with an else-'left' fallback; view/clipboard.ts:181 asOneOf against ALIGNMENTS at :49), confirming the CRDT path is the unguarded weakest entry point. Considered out-of-scope since the write vector needs an edit-permission collaborator using the raw Yorkie SDK rather than the UI, but rejected it: this is XML/template injection with a demonstrably unescaped sink, in-lane, and the uncertainty about the write path belongs in confidence rather than in dropping the finding. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The slides element clipboard still casts an attacker-writable clipboard payload straight to Element[] (which carries docs Block[]), bypassing the new docs sanitizer
finding.evidence: The threat model this change introduces — "the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour is JSON that *any* page can put on the system clipboard … casting it to `Block[]` would let a hostile page write arbitrary values straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters" (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:36-43) — applies verbatim to the slides clipboard, which is not fixed. `deserializeElements` validates only `magic` and `Array.isArray(elements)` and then `return parsed.elements;` (slides/.../clipboard.ts:45-48), with the MIME `web application/x-wafflebase-slides+json` — a web custom format any page can write via `navigator.clipboard.write`. `Element` embeds docs blocks (`packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1` imports `Block` from `@wafflebase/docs`, `:265 blocks: Block[]`), so a hostile payload's arbitrary `headingLevel`, `style.color`, `image.src`, unknown block types and junk keys reach the docs model, renderer and exporters through the slides paste path while the docs paste path is now validated. An added-but-bypassable validation reads as covered; at minimum the slides deserializer should reuse the docs sanitizer for the `blocks` of each text-bearing element.

verdict.reason: Verified in full. packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58 is exactly as described: isPayload checks only `magic === MAGIC` and `Array.isArray(elements)`, then line 48 returns `parsed.elements` typed as Element[] with no shape validation. Element embeds docs blocks (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1 imports Block from @wafflebase/docs; :265 `blocks: Block[]`), so untrusted JSON reaches the docs model. Reachability is confirmed and is in fact broader than the reviewer claimed: MIME_TYPE (clipboard.ts:12) is a `web `-prefixed custom format any page may write via navigator.clipboard.write and is consumed at keyboard.ts:819, AND the text/plain fallbacks at keyboard.ts:827 and :837 feed tryDeserialize -> deserializeElements (:845-851), so a plain writeText of magic-bearing JSON is enough. No downstream guard exists: paste.ts:52-55 spreads `...src` into ElementInit and store/memory.ts:562 does `{ ...clone(init), id }`, normalizing only the id (:561) and connector frame (:587-592). Meanwhile the docs path is hardened — docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:22-30 and :347-360 route through sanitizeBlocks, and the comment at :36-43 states this exact threat model (arbitrary headingLevel, unknown block type, junk keys reaching the shared Yorkie tree, renderer and DOCX/PDF exporters). This is unsafe deserialization / unsafe untrusted-input handling, in-lane, and the classic bypassable-gate pattern where the weakest entry point sits outside the diff. No refutation ground applies.
